offset_convention: Zero-based byte offsets into the Linux installed executable, not source lines. Excerpts are kept only under the raw capture directory. Annotations are investigation inferences from these call paths, not a provider compatibility promise.

entries.annotation: SDK event queue accepts events only in noninteractive mode or with an active REPL bridge.
Resolve ye from the imported launch-options module, rather than from an unrelated minified symbol.
Resolve Du: REPL bridge availability, not an interactive stdout or journal contract.
Normal shell completion awaits output processing, updates task status, claims notification, and then calls enqueuePendingNotification. Task status publication is not journal publication.
Shell notification chooses owner agent or main session and carries task/tool identity; queue stamping adds the run id.
Notification claim stamps notified before enqueue; a prior claim suppresses another notification.
Explicit shell stop stamps killed and notified and emits the SDK terminal event; it does not enqueue the normal root notification. Later normal completion cannot reclaim it.
Interactive enqueue stamps run id, may defer via Ho, mutates queue and notifies subscribers before recording the enqueue operation.
Queue-operation record schema: ordinary enqueue/dequeue need not carry command UUID or run identity.
Queue record publication can be held behind an existing promise and content-hook processing; it is separate from queue state.
Default record callback invokes async ypr without awaiting it; diskless mode does not write this journal.
Queue journal writer is asynchronous.
Journal insert tracks an async append; another-session writes may wait for another queued write.
Ordinary dequeue records lack correlated command identities; removal is not completed notification processing.
Attributed removal records can carry reason, command UUID, delivery ID and content; consumed and discarded paths share this recorder.
Interactive wake router consumes after delivery commit with delivered_to_agent; stopped/resume failure/hook decline have different dispositions.
Sidechain user records can retain joined notification run identities. Does not itself establish complete sidechain settlement.
Interactive presence computes busy from loading/delegated work, not pending notification queue membership.
Shell status derives from live Bash task status; React effect asynchronously writes registry status. Queue length is read separately for dialog/UI handling.
Completed shell tasks stop contributing to shell status independently of notification delivery.
Queued shell notification can instead be consumed as a tool result, with delivered_as_tool_result.
Resumed worker call-path signature binds onDeliveryCommitted to the callback invoked in S23.
Delivery callback is invoked before constructing and dispatching resumed-worker execution; delivery is not the completed answer.
